newsitem.title: CHINA: China interbank market volume up in first half '97.
newsitem.headline: China interbank market volume up in first half '97.

text.p: Average daily turnover on China's local currency interbank market was 2.371 billion yuan in the first half of this year, a year-on-year increase of 28.86 percent, the Shanghai Securities News said on Saturday.
The total trading volume of the Shanghai-based interbank market was 294 billion yuan in the first half, the newspaper said.
It gave no figure for volume in the first half of last year, but the market traded 587.2 billion yuan for the whole of 1996, exchange statistics have showed.

The weighted average rate of the seven contracts on the interbank market was 11.35 percent in the first half of this year, down 1.21 percentage points year on year, the newspaper said. It gave no reasons for the fall.
Shanghai traders have said the fall in the weighted average rate on the market earlier this year was mainly due to two bank interest rate cuts in China in May and August last year.
The seven-day and 60-day contracts were the most actively traded in the first half, the newspaper said. The market also trades one-day, 20-, 30-, 90- and 120-day contracts.
